summary: The x on the desktop composer's 'Follow suggestions are off for this chat' notice is saved per conversation (conversations.follow_notice_dismissed, resolved through resolveRootThreadId), rides on worktree.drift as followNoticeDismissed, and keeps the notice hidden in that chat however many worktrees it works in. Choosing a mode again clears it. The branch picker offers 'Turn Follow suggestions back on' while suggestions are off (read over app:get-conversation-follow-suggestions), so the choice stays reversible. The rule lives in src/shared/follow-suggestions.ts (followSuggestionView's 'hidden' view, followSuggestionsOff). The chip's own x keeps closing only the current suggestion, per the drift watcher's per-turn re-arm.

reactNativeIos.reason: The React Native app does not handle worktree.drift and shows neither the Follow chip nor the off notice; the new optional event field is ignored by it.

nativeAndroid.reason: Native Android shows a drift row from worktreePath and branch only, with no Follow-suggestion modes and no off notice; its decoder reads named fields, so the new optional followNoticeDismissed field is ignored.

automated: npm run build:fast && SB_VISUAL_SCOPE=screens node e2e/visual-regressions.e2e.mjs (2 runs, no baseline changed)
notExercised: The notice's x and the branch picker's 'Turn Follow suggestions back on' were not clicked in the running app; the rule, the reducer and the storage are unit-tested.

Mixed versions were not run. An older desktop ignores the optional event field and keeps the previous behaviour. A newer desktop against an older backend gets a rejected dismiss (logged; the notice comes back as before) and no 'Turn Follow suggestions back on' entry in the branch picker, since that backend lacks the read channel.
